card.needs: Needs: power (red) in a loop, in at plus and out at minus.
card.popularMechanics: A DC motor like this spins the blades of a hand-held fan.

failureModes.cardLine: No complete circuit: the shaft stays still.
failureModes.hint: This motor is not in a loop with the battery pack
failureModes.teachingNote: Current flows only round a complete loop: out of the battery pack, through the motor and back. With one wire missing, nothing flows, so the shaft stays still.

failureModes.cardLine: Too little power: it turns slowly.
failureModes.hint: This motor is not getting enough power
failureModes.teachingNote: Speed rises with voltage. On too little, such as a single cell, the motor turns slowly, and the battery pack drains more for each turn it makes.

failureModes.cardLine: Too much to turn: it stops and hums.
failureModes.hint: This motor cannot turn its load
failureModes.teachingNote: A motor can turn only so much load. Asked for more, such as up a steep ramp or against a wall, the shaft stops and the motor hums while it draws the most current it ever draws, so the battery pack drains fast.

failureModes.cardLine: Wires swapped: it turns the other way.
failureModes.hint: This motor's plus and minus are swapped
failureModes.teachingNote: A DC motor turns one way when its plus meets plus, and the other way when its wires swap. On a robot, one motor wired the other way round spins it on the spot.
